title: Token throughput canary + regression framework for core LLMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create and maintain a lightweight, reproducible tokens-per-second canary and regression framework that runs continuous microbenchmarks against our core model catalog. The goal is to detect regressions in sustained tokens/sec and p95 latency within the CI pipeline and as a periodic background job, provide actionable diffs, and tie regressions to commits, runtime changes, or kernel selection decisions. This ticket covers harness design, canonical workload fingerprints, CI integration, dashboarding, and automated alerting/playbook generation.
acceptance_criteria: Canary harness runs nightly and on PRs for selected core models (gpt-core-v1, redwood-1.0, open-quant) and reports tokens/sec and p95 latency
Regression detector raises alerts when tokens/sec drops >7% or p95 increases >12% relative to the baseline window across two consecutive runs
Benchmarks are reproducible (seeded workloads, pinned model versions, deterministic batching) and results stored in time-series DB with metadata tags
CI job produces a human-readable regression summary with probable culprits (commit list, kernel change, infra region) and links to failing traces and trace IDs
On-call playbook entry created and linked to alerts; runbook includes rollback/fallback guidance and canary rollback automation for Dedicated tier
comments: 2026-02-10 - Created: Initial proposal to unify multiple ad-hoc token-TP benchmarks into a single canary + regression pipeline. Noted overlap with existing nightly smoke tests.

2026-02-18 - Design sync with Runtime team: agreed on canonical workloads (short-chat, long-context summarization, multi-turn Q&A) and sampling proportions. Decided to capture both continuous steady-state and burst microbursts.

2026-02-25 - Spike complete: prototype harness implemented in python using grpc client and local KV warmup. Observed 5% variance across runs; introduced deterministic prompt seeding and KV priming step.
2026-03-03 - PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2345 adds harness scaffolding, prometheus exporter, and baseline collector. Requesting runtime review from @marco and @tara.

2026-03-06 - Review feedback: @marco requested clearer separation of client load generator from runtime-facing probes to avoid resource contention; @tara suggested tagging runs by kernel-profile and quantization to aid triage.
2026-03-09 - Implementation update: Added p95 computation using sliding-window aggregation and histogram buckets; integrated with observability dashboard (grafana link below).

2026-03-11 - Staging results: Nightly canary detected a 9% tokens/sec drop on redwood-1.0 in eu-west-1 after kernel upgrade. Alert created and routed to runtime-oncall. Root cause: kernel selection fallback changed default tiling. Next steps: add guardrail to pin kernel until QA signoff.
